text: Faith is the assurance of what we hope for, the conviction of what we do not see.
It was by faith that the people of old received God's approval.
By faith we understand that the universe was formed by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.

versions.text: By faith we understand that the universe was formed by the word of God, so that what is seen did not come from things that are visible.
versions.explanation: "Did not come from things that are visible" is redundant next to "what is seen" and reads heavily for oral delivery. γεγονέναι carries the sense of "was made/came into being," which the revised wording renders more crisply.

text: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did, and through it he was commended as righteous, since God himself bore witness concerning his gifts. And through his faith he still speaks, though he is dead.
By faith Enoch was taken up, so that he did not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken up he was commended as one who pleased God.
And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever comes to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

By faith Noah, warned by God about things not yet seen, in reverent fear built an ark to save his household. Through it he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.

versions.text: By faith Noah, warned about things not yet seen, took God at his word and built an ark to save his household. By his faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
versions.explanation: εὐλαβηθείς means "moved with reverent/holy fear," a note of godly awe that "took God at his word" flattens into mere belief. Also, χρηματισθείς implies divine warning, which "warned by God" makes explicit.

versions.text: By faith Noah, warned by God about things not yet seen, built an ark in reverent fear to save his household. By his faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
versions.explanation: The feminine relative pronoun ἧς most naturally takes the nearest feminine antecedent, κιβωτόν ("ark"), so "through it" keeps the intended ambiguity of the Greek rather than resolving it to faith, and avoids the stylistic pile-up of "by his faith ... by faith" in one sentence. Moving "in reverent fear" before the verb also lets the participial phrase modify the building action more clearly for a listener, instead of trailing after "ark".

text: By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he would receive as an inheritance; he went out, not knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a stranger in the land of promise, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.
For he was waiting for the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
By faith Sarah herself received power to conceive, even though she was past the age, because she considered him faithful who had made the promise.
And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
All these died in faith. They had not received what was promised, but they saw it and welcomed it from a distance, confessing that they were strangers and sojourners on the earth.
For those who speak this way make it clear that they are looking for a homeland.
If they had been thinking of the land they left behind, they would have had opportunity to return.
But as it is, they long for a better country—a heavenly one. That is why God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his only son,
of whom it had been said, "Through Isaac your offspring shall be named."
He reasoned that God was able even to raise the dead—and figuratively speaking, he did receive him back from death.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, speaking of things to come.
By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, spoke of the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.
By faith Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's edict.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
He chose to be mistreated along with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.
He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.
By faith he left Egypt, unafraid of the king's anger; he persevered as one who sees him who is invisible.
By faith he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as though on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to do so, they were swallowed up.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with the disobedient, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
And what more shall I say? Time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
quenched the fury of flames, escaped the edge of the sword; who were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in battle, and routed foreign armies.
Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured, refusing release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.
Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, mistreated—

versions.text: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, persecuted, mistreated—
versions.explanation: θλιβόμενοι means "afflicted/oppressed" rather than specifically "persecuted" (which would be διωκόμενοι). "Afflicted" is both more accurate and keeps the triple rhythm of the list.

text: the world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.
All of these were commended for their faith, yet none of them received what was promised,
since God had planned something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect apart from us.
